name: Cap cUSD
oneLiner: CUSD is Cap's USD stablecoin minted against a vault basket of regulated stablecoins and tokenized T-bill funds, with EigenLayer-secured AVS coverage.
collateral: Governance-whitelisted basket of regulated dollar-denominated crypto assets: regulated stablecoins (e.g. USDC) and tokenized government money-market funds (e.g. wrapped WisdomTree Government MMF, wWTGXX); idle reserve capital is deployed into US T-bill yield and crypto lending strategies via the protocol's fractional-reserve module. The accepted assets are governance-controlled rather than a fixed list.
pegMechanism: Dynamic-fee vault: users deposit whitelisted reserve assets to mint cUSD at oracle-determined value; redemptions return a proportional basket of all underlying assets, socializing any reserve depeg across redeemers; dynamic interest rates prevent full utilization so redemptions remain atomic; secured by EigenLayer AVS

blacklistabilityReview.evidence: The verified CapToken implementation behind the tracked Ethereum cUSD proxy exposes pauseProtocol() and pauseAsset(), which can halt transfers at the protocol or individual reserve-asset scope. Cap's documentation identifies the tracked cUSD deployment and its governance-controlled vault; the reviewed source therefore establishes direct system-wide transfer-pause capability for cUSD. Reserve and route dependencies add separate upstream exposure.
blacklistabilityReview.reviewer: SONG Safety Score V9 access review

review.evidence: Live RPC and verified implementation review resolved the prior enumeration blocker. Ethereum's vault points to an external AccessControlEnumerableUpgradeable proxy; selector-derived upgrade/addAsset/setDepositCap roles each had exactly the one-day Timelock as holder. Ethereum, MegaETH, and Tempo governance converge on the same 3/5 Safe. Tempo event history and current role calls identified the active issuer proxy and the current timelocked DEFAULT_ADMIN.

applicabilityBasis.summary: cUSD is USD-pegged and vault-redeemable at ~1:1, which superficially resembles a payment stablecoin, but its proportional basket redemption mechanism (socializing losses across redeemers), absence of a disclosed legal issuer entity, and the protocol's self-description as code-enforced rather than institutionally backed create genuine ambiguity about whether a legal 'permitted issuer' exists under the GENIUS Act definition. The stcUSD product separates yield; cUSD itself does not natively pay yield.

genius.notes: Cap documents basket-based vault redemption rather than a clean fiat issuer redemption promise. No legal entity is publicly disclosed as the issuer. The protocol operates code-enforced protection without named regulatory oversight. Until a legal issuer entity is disclosed and pathway to GENIUS compliance clarified, applicability remains unclear.

negativeEvidenceReview.summary: Cap Protocol has no publicly disclosed GENIUS authorization, application, or state-qualified status; no legal issuer entity is named in public documentation; basket redemption design diverges from GENIUS payment-stablecoin model; no PPSI application framework exists yet.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: Cap cUSD uses LayerZero OFT/Stargate-style omnichain routing for multichain deployments rather than Across intent/liquidity bridging. Because durable cross-chain supply depends on the external OFT messaging stack, Pharos scores the route as external lock/mint exposure.
